cards.name: Boost gauge and speed surge
cards.summary: Holding boost spends a shared 0-90 gauge to add forward speed and pull the chase camera back, with a forced cooldown at the ceiling.
cards.behavior: While boost is held without brake, the ship adds two speed units every update up to thirty above cruise speed, and the gauge fills by three units per update on rails or one and a half in an arena. Reaching ninety gauge units latches a cooldown, and once both keys are up the gauge only recovers at half a unit per update on rails or 0.35 in an arena, so boost is a burst that must be paid back. The camera distance target slides to 400 units of extra setback with a thirty-unit-per-update approach limit, and the contrail grows 0.04 scale units per update up to 0.6. The same routine also ages the loop arming and boost-press timers, so a port that fires boost every update must still model the recovery lag and the cooldown latch.

cards.name: Brake and reverse thrust
cards.summary: Braking fills the same gauge to slow the ship below cruise speed and pulls the chase camera in towards the hull.
cards.behavior: Braking drains three gauge units per update on rails and one and a half in an arena, subtracting one speed unit per update down to a floor of twenty units below cruise speed, so the ship can hang back or drift backwards relative to the streaming course. The gauge saturates at ninety and latches a cooldown, and while the key is up it recovers at half a unit per update on rails or 0.35 in an arena, with the negative speed returning towards zero at half a unit per update. The camera distance target moves to 180 units while braking, which shortens the chase distance instead of lengthening it. On planet levels the four flap surfaces swing to ninety degrees so the wing silhouette reads the drag.

cards.name: Double-tap barrel roll
cards.summary: Two presses of one shoulder button inside ten updates spin the hull through a full roll with a speed bonus and a forced turn rate.
cards.behavior: Each shoulder press starts a ten-update window; a second press inside that window upgrades the usual bank into a roll and records a thirty-degree-per-update spin for ten updates. After the spin timer runs out the rate decays by five degrees per update until it reaches zero, and a blur alpha rises by a hundred per update to a cap of 180 before bleeding off thirty per update. While the roll is live the lateral and vertical velocity is scaled by 1.5 and, on rails, the yaw rate is pinned to 6.9 degrees per update, so a roll doubles as a hard turn rather than a cosmetic spin. A port needs the ten-update input window, the fixed spin rate and the decay tail, not an instant snap to the target angle.

cards.name: Banking and shoulder-button attitude
cards.summary: Shoulder buttons set a ninety-degree bank target that the hull chases, and the current bank angle feeds turn authority and ground clearance.
cards.behavior: Holding one shoulder button while the other is free drives the bank target to ninety degrees, and the opposite button drives it to minus ninety; with neither held the target returns to zero. The bank chases its target with 0.1 or 0.2 of the remaining angle per update and a ten-degree-per-update limit, so a full bank takes several updates instead of one. Once the bank passes ten degrees in the turn direction the yaw rate doubles and the smoothing fraction loosens to 0.2, which is what gives a banked turn its bite. Within seventy units of the ground the hull is lifted six units per update while a bank is held, a small anti-stall cushion. A ship with one wing broken keeps a permanent seventeen-degree bank bias away from the intact wing even with no input.

cards.name: Stick shaping, pitch and roll authority
cards.summary: Stick deflection is scaled and rotated by the current bank, then fed into smoothed yaw, pitch and roll targets with a pitch clamp near the ground.
cards.behavior: The stick vector is scaled to three quarters and rotated by the current bank so a banked ship still answers the player's intent. Yaw chases the scaled horizontal deflection times 0.68 with a 2.3-degree-per-update rate and a 0.1 smoothing fraction; banked past ten degrees into the turn the rate doubles and the fraction rises to 0.2. Pitch chases negative stick Y with the same rate, but a downward request inside fifty units of the ground is zeroed and its fraction is loosened to 0.2, which keeps the ship off the floor. Roll chases stick X times 0.6, scaled by 1.5 in arena flight or 1.0 on rails, 0.8 within seventy units of the ground, and 0.1 while exactly one shoulder button is held, with a one-degree rate when the stick is centred and four degrees when it is not. On rails the resulting lateral and vertical velocity components are spread by 1.4 to widen the turn, so the same stick input carves differently in the two modes.

cards.name: Somersault loop
cards.summary: A forward-then-back stick motion with a boost press starts a full pitch loop that lifts the ship and refills the boost gauge.
cards.behavior: Pushing the stick forward keeps a five-update arming window topped up; pulling the stick back lets that window run down, and a boost press while it sits between one and four starts a somersault. During the loop the pitch value climbs towards 360 degrees at five degrees per update with a 0.1 fraction, and the loop clears once it passes 350 degrees, restoring the saved view state on rails or resetting the camera easing in an arena. The first half of the arc lifts the ship two units per update while the pitch is under 180 degrees, which keeps the loop above the course, and the boost gauge refills by two units per update on rails or one in an arena while boosting is locked out. The four flap surfaces swing to sixty degrees going up and minus fifty coming down.

cards.name: On-rails path progress
cards.summary: The course scrolls by integrating forward speed into a path coordinate that wraps after 500000 units while the ship stays inside a corridor.
cards.behavior: The path coordinate advances by the negated forward velocity every update and is published as the world scroll used by geometry and texture animation, so the ship stays near the origin while the course streams past. Outside a boss fight, a coordinate beyond 500000 units resets the path to zero and clears spawned objects, which is how a very long stage recycles its space. The lateral and vertical path targets chase the path speed scaled by 0.54 with a two-unit-per-update limit, so corners lean in gradually. The ship is then hard-clamped to a corridor of 700 units half width, 680 units of headroom on planet levels or 612 in space, and a floor of 544 units below the path in space or 40 units above the ground elsewhere. A warning flag is raised 100 units inside each edge before the clamp actually stops the ship.

cards.name: Laser fire cadence
cards.summary: A fresh press fires at once and holding fire repeats every fourth update while each bolt advances in four sub-steps per update.
cards.behavior: A fresh press fires immediately and loads an eight-update cooldown; while the button is held the counter decrements and a bolt is released whenever the low two bits of the counter are clear, which works out to one bolt every fourth update. Bolts leave at the nose with a 1.2-update lead along their velocity, and twin or upgraded fire drops the muzzle by ten units so the two barrels read separately. The bolt asks for a speed of 400 units split by three, and laser bolts are stepped four times per update before collision, so the visible bolt covers about four times its per-step distance each update and its thirty-five-tick life counter drains at the same four-times rate. A broken wing forces every shot back to single fire, and the muzzle flash scale grows from 0.5 to 0.75 for the upgraded pair.

cards.name: Charge and lock release
cards.summary: Holding fire charges a counter to 21, launches search projectiles every fourth update, and releases a homing shot when the button comes up.
cards.behavior: Holding fire raises a charge counter that saturates at 21, with a search tone at 20. Once the counter passes 20 the ship launches a search projectile every fourth update that scans for a target, but both shoulder buttons held suppress that launch so a deliberate charge cannot steal a lock. Releasing the button after the counter passes 10 spends the charge on a homing shot: if a target is already marked the shot fires at once, and if nothing is marked the release still fires because the charge passed 10 before the counter is cleared. The homing shot leaves at seventy units per update with a thirty-update life, and rumble is requested for five updates on every release. A short tap below the charge threshold clears the counter without firing.

cards.name: Lock-on target tracking
cards.summary: A search projectile claims the nearest active target inside a 300-unit box on rails or 200 in an arena, then the homing shot steers towards it.
cards.behavior: A search projectile tests active targets against an axis-aligned box of 300 units on rails and 200 units in an arena, ignores anything already marked, and stamps the target with a twenty-update marker before reporting a hit and removing every other search projectile. The homing shot then recomputes yaw and pitch towards the marked point every update and steers with an angle rate that ramps three degrees per update up to a ceiling of 360 degrees, refreshing its own life to thirty updates while the target survives. Speed ramps 13 units per update towards 169 once the mark is lost and about eight units per update towards 91 while it is tracking, and the final velocity is that speed plus forty units along the aim vector. With no marked target left the shot coasts, stops steering and keeps its last heading until its life runs out.

cards.name: Smart bomb launch
cards.summary: Pressing the bomb button spends one bomb and launches a slow projectile that needs a marked target before it will leave the ship.
cards.behavior: The bomb button is only honoured when the ship still holds a bomb, the single bomb slot is free, and something is currently marked as a target. The press decrements the bomb count, launches the projectile at 180 units per update with an effect scale of thirty, and starts the flight sound. When the release comes from a charged lock-on instead, the projectile leaves at sixty units per update so it can follow the mark. In split-screen play the count is zeroed rather than decremented, so a bomb is effectively one shot per life. The projectile occupies the last shot slot, which is why the ship cannot launch a second bomb until the first is resolved.

cards.name: Shield pool and hit response
cards.summary: Shields start at 255, absorb damage at two points per update, and every hit sets an invulnerability window, a knockback and a radio callout.
cards.behavior: The ship starts with 255 shield points, and three gold rings raise the cap to 383. A hit stores its damage value, then drains two shield points and two pending damage points per update until both are gone; healing mirrors that at two points per update up to the cap. Every hit sets a twenty-update hit timer and an invulnerability window that is twenty updates by default, five near some bosses and three in the final arena, which is also the window that gates further collision tests. Knockback is twenty units along the hit direction, or twenty plus 0.3 times the current boost speed for heavy hits, and expert mode doubles the incoming damage. Shield warnings are keyed to fractions of the pool, with the softer alarm below 100 points and the harsher one below 50.

cards.name: Wing integrity and broken wings
cards.summary: Each wing carries 60 integrity points that side hits chew by 20 and vertical hits by 15, and a broken wing bends the ship's velocity.
cards.behavior: Both wings start with 60 integrity points, or 10 in expert mode. A hit from the side removes 20 points from that wing, while a hit from above or below removes 15 from a randomly chosen wing; the wing flash runs 30 updates and the debris timer 50. When a wing reaches zero it counts as broken, spawns debris and smoke, and schedules a repair 1000 updates later. A broken wing bends the flight path in a direction that depends on the mode: in arena flight a 2.5-unit sideways and downward bias is added to the local velocity before the orientation matrix, so a broken right wing pushes the ship sideways one way and down while a broken left wing pushes it the other way and down, and on rails the same 2.5 units are applied directly in world space. The hull also keeps a permanent seventeen-degree bank bias and the flaps sit at the broken-wing angle, so the damage reads without a HUD.

cards.name: Ground scrape and scenery collision
cards.summary: Hull probes below 13 units over the ground take damage, and scenery is only tested inside a cull radius and after the mercy window expires.
cards.behavior: Two hull probes at the wing roots are compared against a plane thirteen units above the ground; on solid ground a scrape deals 21 damage, while over water the ship skims with a seven-update hit timer and a pitch rate of half its current total speed. Scenery collision is skipped entirely while the mercy window is live, which is the same window that a hit opens, so one impact cannot cascade into a dozen more in the same frame. In all-range arenas scenery is tested only within 1100 units horizontally, widened to 4000 units for a couple of large stages, and on rails the test is limited to scenery whose depth lies within 2000 units of the ship. Passing close to scenery raises a whoosh counter by two up to a cap of four, which is the port's cue to play a near-miss effect.

cards.name: On-rails chase camera
cards.summary: The rail camera sits 400 units in front of the origin, follows the ship's offset from the path, and rolls partly with the ship.
cards.behavior: The eye sits 400 units in front of the origin and looks at the ship's path position one unit short of the current coordinate, so forward speed reads as the world streaming towards the camera. The ship's offset from the path is scaled by roughly 0.78 before it drives the eye and look target, which keeps the ship near the centre while it moves. Stick deflection shifts the look target through a 1.6-unit yaw coupling and, in space, a 0.8-unit pitch coupling; near the ground the pitch coupling drops to 0.3 and the eye keeps a constant fifty-unit lift over the path offset, so the camera does not scrape the floor. A loop lifts the eye by 200 units and relaxes the vertical smoothing, and the camera roll takes 0.3 of the ship's roll on planets and 0.2 in space. The cockpit view projects its look target 1000 units straight ahead and copies the full bank plus the rock angle into the roll.

cards.name: All-range chase camera
cards.summary: The arena camera trails the ship by a distance that boost and brake move, and rolls with yaw instead of copying it exactly.
cards.behavior: In an arena the eye sits a base 300 units behind the ship along its yaw, adjusted by the camera distance that boost and brake drive, and a loop adds 500 units so the arc stays in frame; the alternate view pushes the eye out to 1000 units. Eye height is 50 units above the scaled ship height, reduced by 1.5 times the smoothed stick pitch offset, and the look target sits at 0.79 of the ship height so the camera looks slightly down the hull. The look target also takes a yaw offset of twice the ship's yaw with a two-degree-per-update limit, and the camera rolls to minus 0.3 of that yaw offset, which is what sells a hard bank in an arena. The eye smoothing fraction decays towards 0.2 and the vertical look smoothing also settles at 0.2, while the horizontal look target keeps a fraction of 1.0, so a cut snaps horizontally and glides vertically.
